subject: Live advisory: EU generation latency and streaming truncation event
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lilycode.com>, ops@lilycode.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Oct 2028 07:48:00 +0000
Subject: Live advisory: EU generation latency and streaming truncation event

Hi Alex / LilyCode ops team —

Quick interim advisory: we’re seeing an elevated p95 latency and a small number of streaming truncations for hosted generation endpoints in our eu-west-1 region (affecting v1/generate and v1/chat/completions).

What we saw
- Window: ~07:30–08:20 UTC (initial spike at 07:30, partial mitigation at ~08:15).
- Symptom: p95 for generation requests rose from ~380ms to ~1.6s; ~0.8% of streaming requests observed early truncation / partial bodies.
- Scope: multi-tenant hosted API customers in eu-west-1; roughly 4–6% of requests routed through a degraded worker pool during the spike.

What we’re doing now
- We activated guarded multi-path routing to avoid the degraded pool and scaled an alternate capacity pool; routing changes show mitigation starting ~08:15 UTC.
- Engineers are collecting KV cache / routing metrics and tracing affected request flows for root cause.
- We’ve opened a high-priority investigation and will send a postmortem with timeline and corrective actions.

Immediate customer impact and recommendations
- If you observe incomplete streaming chunks, a safe client mitigation is to retry idempotently (same input) — upstream dedupe checks will apply.
- Embeddings and non-streaming endpoints are not expected to be affected by this event (we’re confirming but preliminary checks show normal metrics for those routes).

Links and attachments
- Status page incident: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/EU-2028-10-22-routing-degradation
- Attachment: incident-brief.pdf (short summary + current metrics snapshot)

We’ll post a detailed timeline and root cause analysis in our next update (target within 4 hours). Apologies for the disruption — we know low-latency streaming is important for your product.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-brief.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Live advisory: EU generation latency and streaming truncation event

Thanks Neha — appreciate the heads-up. Quick questions:

1) Are embeddings (v1/embeddings) completely unaffected? We have background indexing jobs running and want to confirm no lag.
2) Can you confirm whether token usage/charge accounting will be impacted by retries customers may do?

We’re seeing deliberate user-facing errors for ~5% of active sessions in eu-west-1 (our error budget dashboard spiked). If you can share an ETA for the postmortem timeline that helps our incident bridge.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform — LilyCode
On Mon, 22 Oct 2028 at 07:48, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick interim advisory: we’re seeing an elevated p95 latency and a small number of streaming truncations for hosted generation endpoints in our eu-west-1 region...
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lilycode.com>, ops@lilycode.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Oct 2028 09:10:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Live advisory: EU generation latency and streaming truncation event

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the details. Answers below.

1) Embeddings: confirmed NOT impacted. Our telemetry shows normal p50/p95 for v1/embeddings across eu-west-1 for the entire window. The cause appears scoped to the generation-serving path and streaming assembly pipeline only.

2) Token accounting / billing: retry attempts from clients that result in duplicate successful completions will be deduplicated on our end if the same request-id is provided; otherwise retries that return additional tokens will be billed normally. We will offer a discrete credit for verified user-facing failures arising from this event — we’ll coordinate the list of affected tenants and propose credits in the postmortem.

Preliminary root cause (investigation notes)
- Trigger: an orchestration edge-case caused a transient cache invalidation for a subset of generation workers when a rolling kernel selection change coincided with a cache eviction job.
- Effect: some requests were routed to recently-evicted workers which incurred elevated cold-path latency and a partial streaming assembly race resulting in truncation.
- Mitigation applied: guarded multi-path routing + expedited warm-up of alternate worker pool; we also disabled the immediate cache eviction job that coincided with the kernel rollout.

We’ve attached the incident-timeline.csv with event timestamps from control plane, routing, and worker metrics. The postmortem draft will include the timeline, root cause, and our remediation plan (fixes to orchestrator guardrails and an autoscaler change to avoid similar transient evictions).

ETA / next steps
- Postmortem draft (internal + customer summary): targeted delivery by 12:00 UTC today.
- Customer-facing summary + action items (final): by end-of-day tomorrow.

I’ll keep you updated in this thread and post the draft to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/incidents/LILY-2028-10-22-postmortem

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Oct 2028 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — EU routing degradation (final)

Hi Alex / LilyCode team —

This is the final customer-facing summary for the eu-west-1 routing degradation that affected generation endpoints on 2028-10-22. Thank you for your patience and for raising the impact to our attention.

Summary (what happened)
- Event window: 07:30–08:20 UTC. Root cause: race between a kernel-selection rollout and a scheduled KV cache eviction job that led to transient worker pool evictions and elevated cold-path latency for a subset of generation workers.
- Impact: elevated p95 latency (up to ~1.6s) and early truncation for ~0.8% of streaming requests. A small portion (~4–6%) of generation traffic was routed through the affected pool during the window. Embeddings and non-streaming APIs were not materially impacted.

Remediation (what we did)
- Immediate: activated guarded multi-path routing; scaled alternate warm pools; disabled the colliding cache eviction job; rolled back the kernel-selection rollout for the affected subpopulation.
- Short-term fixes (deployed within 24 hours): orchestrator guardrail to serialize kernel selection with eviction jobs; safer warm-up path for worker pools; improved tracing for streaming assembly.
- Long-term actions (target Q1 2029): extend autoscaler hysteresis to avoid evictions during kernel rollouts; add a canary for streaming assembly changes; automated incident-runbook updates.

Customer remediation and credits
- We will validate affected tenant request logs and propose a one-time service credit to customers who experienced confirmed user-facing truncations / errors during the window. Neha will coordinate credits and impacted tenant lists.

Where to find more details
- Full postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/incidents/LILY-2028-10-22-postmortem
- Public status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/EU-2028-10-22-routing-degradation
- Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf, incident-timeline.csv

If you’d like a short bridge to walk through the timeline and our mitigations, we’re happy to schedule one. Thanks again — we’re prioritizing preventing recurrence.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
